newsitem.title: USA: Illegal Mexican maids busted in hotel raids.
newsitem.headline: Illegal Mexican maids busted in hotel raids.

text.p: Sixty-seven illegal immigrants employed as maids have been arrested in three days of raids on hotels and motels in Albuquerque, New Mexico, officials said on Thursday.

The maids, all of them Mexican citizens, were arrested between Tuesday and Thursday at about 20 hotels and motels by U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service agents as part of a crackdown on undocumented workers.
Last month, several mariachi musicians were arrested in the Texas border town of El Paso and sent back to Mexico.

"The INS is committed to ensuring that legal workers do not have to compete for jobs with workers who do not have the legal right to them," said Luis Garcia, INS director for the El Paso district which includes New Mexico.

INS spokesman Dan Kane said the maids all agreed to return to Mexico voluntarily and an investigation was under way to determine if the hotels and motels -- which include Holiday Inn, Best Western, Ramada Inn and Super 8 Motel -- will be fined for employing undocumented workers.
Fines can range from $250 to $2,000 per worker. Kane said the average wage paid to the maids was $5.50 an hour.
